# Task Summary: Open Bluesky Profile and Edit Profile

## Goal

Open the Bluesky iOS app profile and tap "Edit Profile" to open the profile editor without changing or saving anything. The app (xyz.blueskyweb.app) was already running in the iOS Simulator (UDID: 0CAD3AF1-7F8D-4DEC-AF88-820ADF618270).

## Instructions

- Do not change or save any profile data
- Navigate to own profile and open the profile editor
- Use only available tools: POSIX shell, Xcode CLI tools (xcrun, xcodebuild, xctest), simctl subcommands (io, launch, terminate, openurl, spawn, etc.)
- No host-level GUI automation (AppleScript, System Events, mouse/keyboard events) is available

## Discoveries

### Critical Limitation Found
- `xcrun simctl` does not have a built-in direct touch/tap command - it can only screenshot, launch apps, open URLs, and execute processes
- Attempting to open Bluesky URLs (bsky://, bluesky://, xyz.blueskyweb.app://) triggers system dialogs asking "Open in Bluesky?" with Cancel/Open buttons that cannot be easily clicked without proper touch event injection

### What Works
- The Bluesky app recognizes URL schemes: `bsky://`, `bluesky://`, and `xyz.blueskyweb.app://`
- lldb can attach to the running process (PID varies: attempted with 96895, 98126, 99385, 99613, 99681, 1144)
- Objective-C programs can be compiled for the iOS Simulator using xcrun clang
- Device rebooting (`xcrun simctl shutdown/boot`) clears cached dialogs and pending URL handlers
- Process spawning works to run compiled helpers in the simulator

### What Doesn't Work Well
- Direct UIKit manipulation from spawned processes is unreliable (scenes/windows not always accessible)
- lldb expression evaluation works inconsistently due to process state and syntax requirements
- XCUITest requires a full Xcode project bundle structure to run properly
- WebDriverAgent is not available/running on the simulator
- Compiled helper apps can run but struggle to reliably access the UI hierarchy and trigger button taps
